bindings.label: Sudden onset pain and redness in the right eye, with photophobia

83-year-old Caucasian male farmer, known for 3 months to have a hypermature cataract in the right eye and a mature cataract in the left eye, scheduled for cataract extraction in the left eye first followed by the right eye; no history of ocular trauma or previous ocular surgery; no relevant family history or ophthalmological conditions; not on any topical or systemic medication
During preoperative consultation for left eye cataract surgery, he reported acute ocular pain and photophobia in the right eye that began a few days prior

Clinical examination showed visual acuity of light perception in the right eye and counting fingers in the left eye; intraocular pressure was 50 mmHg in the right eye and 13 mmHg in the left eye; slit lamp biomicroscopy of the right eye revealed circumciliary congestion, diffuse corneal edema, pseudohypopyon, complete lens opacification, and suspended white particles in the anterior chamber and pupillary area
B-scan shows a hyper-reflective vitreous band in the right eye
B-scan shows no major posterior pathology
